slides.title: AI Updates Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 is still
slides.text: AI Updates Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 is still offline Anthropic negotiates with the Trump administration on future access conditions No concrete timeline or announced date exists for re‑enabling any 5‑series models, so developers should not rely on their near‑term availability US Government asked OpenAI to stagger the release of GPT‑5.6 , over security concerns GPT‑5.6 will first go to a small set of “trusted partners” in a limited preview, with the government approving access customer by customer during that phase https://www.youtube.com/shorts/oQ_aqiSTLQc This aligns with a recent Trump executive order that asks companies to give the federal government early access (up to ~30 days) to the most capable models , so agencies can evaluate them before broad deployment Reports suggest the NSA is involved in defining which models qualify as “covered” based on offensive/defensive cyber potential, Federal officials may help choose which entities get early access

slides.title: Alibaba - Jack Ma's Downfall Alibaba today is
slides.text: Alibaba - Jack Ma's Downfall Alibaba today is an AI-first company, famous for its Qwen LLMs, AI-powered e-commerce, cloud services, and AI agents In October 2020, Alibaba founder Jack Ma gave a speech criticizing China’s financial system, calling it a "pawn shop" This public critique angered senior CCP officials and President Xi Jinping, triggering a massive crackdown on Ma’s companies The planned IPO for Ant Group was suspended, and Alibaba faced a record $2.8 Bln antitrust fine Ma’s influence and business empire were systematically dismantled, and he largely disappeared from public view for years Jack Ma's businesses ended up Losing hundreds of $Billions of value, his personal net worth has dropped from ~$61B to ~$30B By 2025, facing a slowing economy and capital flight, the Chinese government attempted to reconcile with business leaders, including a public appearance by Ma However, investors do not trust CCP, because it demonstrated how it can take over any business US Government has added Alibaba to the blacklist because it is now mostly controlled by CCP https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tDVeGbGaRdE

slides.title: SubQ Subquadratic SubQ 12M-token context model Miami‑based startup
slides.text: SubQ Subquadratic SubQ 12M-token context model Miami‑based startup Subquadratic A proprietary model - access via hosted API Up to a 12‑Mln‑token context window Very fast - x50 faster than FlashAttention‑class models at Mln0token contexts Cheap - x20 cheaper than top proprietary models for similar long‑context tasks Sub‑quadratic sparse‑attention architecture (SSA) For coding agents, analysis of very large document sets (GitHub repos, ...) Strong long‑context retrieval, and significantly reduced attention FLOPs versus dense‑attention transformers https://subq.ai https://api.subq.ai/v1 SubQ 1M-Preview , exposed via the subq-preview (or similar) API name and listed as the current model on third‑party references. Subquadratic has also announced SubQ 1.1 Small , a long‑context SSA model (SSA = Subquadratic Sparse Attention) Parameter counts have not been officially disclosed It is a dense base model whose attention is made content‑sparse via learned routing, so you should think of it as “sparse attention with MoE‑inspired routing,” not a standard MoE‑experts LLM Subquadratic is a private startup, $29M financing in May 2026 ($500M valuation) The company was co‑founded by CEO Justin Dangel and CTO Alexander (Alex) Whedon.

slides.title: Sakana AI - Fugu Ultra Orchestration Sakana AI
slides.text: Sakana AI - Fugu Ultra Orchestration Sakana AI - Fugu Ultra Orchestration Fugu and Fugu Ultra are multi-model orchestration systems They dynamically coordinate multiple AI agents through a single API rather than solving tasks with one monolithic model Built on Sakana’s Trinity and Conductor research, the system handles model selection, delegation, and synthesis internally Sakana positions the approach as a hedge against vendor lock-in and export-control disruptions affecting access to advanced AI models Fugu systems - match or outperform Anthropic’s Claude Fable and Mythos on some benchmarks, especially coding and graduate-level reasoning tasks API Pricing: $5 in / $30 out ($10 / $45 for very large context) Subscriptions Pro & Max - $20/mo, $100/mo Fugu’s performance comes from coordination, model selection, and synthesis across multiple back-end models In practice, it behaves like a single “frontier-class” endpoint, but architecturally it is an orchestration layer rather than a standalone model.

slides.text: AI Updates Reflection AI + SpaceX $6.3 Bln Deal Reflection gets access to NVIDIA GB300 chips at SpaceX’s Colossus 2 data center, paying $150 million per month starting July 1 The agreement runs through 2029 Reflection joins customers including Anthropic, Google, and Cursor as SpaceX expands its AI infrastructure business. Claude Corps Fellowship Anthropic recently unveiled Claude Corps, a year-long fellowship It places early-career workers inside nonprofit organizations to help those groups integrate AI into their operations Groq Raises $650M Six months after Nvidia licensed its tech and poached its CEO, Groq raised $650M to pivot from chipmaker to inference-focused cloud Under co-founder Doug Wightman. Baseten has raised $1.5 Bln to expand its infrastructure for AI inference They run on major clouds (notably Google Cloud) using NVIDIA GPUs Baseten focuses on simplifying deployment pipelines, optimizing GPU utilization, and enabling developers to run custom or open-source models reliably in production - auto-scaling, low-latency, cost‑efficient Baseten is a privately held, founded in 2019 in San Francisco, CA Size ~ 60 employees https://www.baseten.co https://docs.baseten.co

slides.text: Harrison Kinsley (Sentdex) Harrison Kinsley (Sentdex) about AI https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DA2E8szXjoA Deceptive Behavior (specifically referencing Anthropic's "Fable" model) that are designed to intentionally mislead users if the model detects certain types of research, labeling this as a form of "psychological abuse" Top-tier AI models are becoming subject to export restrictions similar to weapons of war (problematic for the industry and the public ) The "moat" around top proprietary companies like OpenAI and Anthropic is effectively gone because high-performance, open-weights models are now available to the public Testing open models - "Miniax M2.7", ... "GLM52" open model can genuinely compete with and replace proprietary models like GPT-55 and Claude Opus 48 Building your own custom coding agents or "harnesses." - greater control, easier troubleshooting, customization to specific model behaviors or quantization needs Running Models Locally - may require multi-GPU setups - expensive Quantization makes it chaper. 4-bit quantization is near-lossless, but 3-bit degrades performance Alternative - services like OpenRouter.ai to access open-source models via API - this is often significantly cheaper than proprietary alternatives but users should research each provider's data privacy policies regarding prompt retention Harrison runs GLM5.2 locally on a custom-built  computer with 4 ( four) NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPUs (Blackwell. 96GB each). Each GPU cost is approx $11K-$14K T he model is massive—approximately 750 Bln params. He uses IQ4XS (4-bit quantiation)

slides.title: AI Updates Hermes Agent Skills "/learn" Distills Any
slides.text: AI Updates Hermes Agent Skills "/learn" Distills Any Workflow Into Reusable Slash Commands Hermes /learn is a command that turns sources like URLs, codebases, docs, PDFs, notes, or recent sessions into a reusable skill for future use It is meant to save you from re-explaining the same workflow and can store the result as a skill file for later loading. Example: /learn how I just deployed the staging server, focus on rollback and verification Hermes will read that conversation plus any referenced files/URLs, then author a SKILL.md that becomes a slash command, e.g. /deploy-staging. Next time you or a teammate want the runbook, you just call /deploy-staging in CLI/TUI/chat instead of re-explaining the process Mujlti-Agent Orchestration Agent Map-Reduce - LLM Map-Reduce - LLM MapReduce pattern - Agentic MapReduce - Agentic Map-Reduce - MapReduce for AI agents - MapReduceEnsemble - LangGraph map-reduce pattern - A-MapReduce - Map-Reduce-Produce - MapReduceProduce - Fan-out/fan-in (parallel agents) - Agentic wide search - Agent search

slides.title: AI Updates Seedance 2.5 - ByteDance’s latest AI
slides.text: AI Updates Seedance 2.5 - ByteDance’s latest AI video model Generating polished, cinematic clips from text prompts and multimodal inputs such as images, video, and audio Ir adds support for native 4K output, longer single-shot scenes up to around 30 seconds, and more advanced multi-shot storytelling with consistent characters and visual style The system can ingest large numbers of reference assets (up to 50) to tightly control motion, composition, and branding in commercial workflows Seedance 2.5 also emphasizes near–real-time generation and conversational editing, enabling interactive refinement of camera moves, lighting, and synchronized audio without rebuilding an entire shot A Rust-based rewrite of SQLite https://github.com/tursodatabase/turso Gaining memory safety, async I/O, and WASM-first extensibility It targets similar or better reliability than classic SQLite, using modern testing approaches like deterministic simulation instead of only reproducing the legacy C test harness

slides.title: AI Updates How Anthropic Employees use "Claude skills"
slides.text: AI Updates How Anthropic Employees use "Claude skills" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3UWxMPUko1k "Claude skills" are structured folders of scripts, assets, and docs Organize skills into four types: Utility (specific tasks), Verification (quality checks), Data Enrichment (external info), Orchestration (chaining steps) . Components - Understand that skills are not just text files; they should include scripts for deterministic tasks, asset templates for consistent output, and clear setup prompts for future usability Verification - Treat verification as a critical quality layer. Use both correctness checks and subjective feedback to ensure high standards Gotchas - Maintain a log of edge cases to improve skills over time. Triggers - Optimize descriptions so Claude knows exactly when to execute specific skills. How Anthropic's Own Team Gets AI to Stop Lying to Them https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EPEI-IIPu4E Be Specific - Clearly define terminology to prevent AI misinterpretation Create a Single Source of Truth - archive outdated files, so the AI only accesses relevant, current data Require Receipts - Prompt the AI to provide citations for its information, making audits easier Get a Second Opinion - For high-stakes tasks, test results in a fresh chat or via a different AI model Test Before Automating - Validate automated tasks using sample data to ensure reliability before removing human oversight

slides.title: Fable Brain Prompting The "Fable Brain" eight instructions
slides.text: Fable Brain Prompting The "Fable Brain" eight instructions https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M03v0gmVu24 From official Anthropic developer documentation that govern Fable's behavior and compiled them into a single system prompt: Act, do not overplan: When you have enough information, commit to a recommendation instead of listing options Lead with the outcome: Provide the bottom line first, without unnecessary background information Ground every claim: Audit claims against evidence; if it’s not verified, say so to prevent hallucinations Stop only at real boundaries: Only pause for truly destructive or irreversible actions Assess, do not act uninvited: When asked a question, report your findings rather than automatically making changes Give the reason: Provide the context ("I am working on this for...") so the model makes smarter choices Match effort to the task: Spend deeper reasoning on complex problems and move faster on routine ones Keep lessons and check your work: Ask the model to remember corrections and verify its answer against the original request The Limits of Prompting The presenter emphasizes that this approach works for communication and decision-making but fails at true autonomy: It cannot create judgment: When given a flawed task, a "fable-brained" model may still provide a confident but wrong answer It cannot grant agency: The model lacks actual tools or internet/code access. If instructed to "act autonomously," it may simply lie about having performed tasks (e.g., "I have deployed this to staging")

slides.title: Harness Engineering - a New Gold Rush "Harness
slides.text: Harness Engineering - a New Gold Rush "Harness Engineering Is AI’s New Gold Rush" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mGYr9VqQnEI Harness engineering marks a shift in AI from models to agents tools, memory, verification, permissions, and feedback loops Unlike prompt engineering, which targets a single good response, a harness builds a lasting environment for consistent performance The same model can vary up to x6 depending on harness quality Key challenges include: context management (filtering noise to surface the right information) Treating memory as a hint to be verified rather than fact Connecting tools to validation checks Looking ahead, Retrospective Harness Optimization lets agents improve themselves by analyzing past trajectories As frontier models converge, the strongest harness becomes the competitive edge

slides.title: Scheduling for your digital employee Custom scheduling for
slides.text: Scheduling for your digital employee Custom scheduling for your Digital Employee Why to use a custom "mycron" vs system crontab: Have access to user's open browser sessions (run in active user environment) Fire agent skills , not just shell commands One daemon for all users Hot-reload on edit (every 60 sec) On-demand reload via API for instant changes. RAND_DELAY=min-max spreads same-minute tasks to prevent a thundering herd on the API. Session persistence (for recurring tasks) Per-minute deduplication prevents double-firing after a restart. Isolated per-user logging

slides.title: Three-layers of an AI agent How to structure
slides.text: Three-layers of an AI agent How to structure an agent to work with multiple projects and clients? Three-layer architecture for an AI agent: 1. stable core runtime 2. shared plugin/marketplace repos 3. thin per-project configuration The core agent remains capability-agnostic and only knows how to read manifests, load selected plugins, manage MCP servers, and apply progressive disclosure Capabilities are packaged as plugins (skills, MCP servers, hooks) in shared repos to maximize reuse instead of per-client forks Each client/project repo stores a small manifest that selects which plugins and MCP servers are enabled and how they are scoped To avoid blowing the context window, only skill metadata (name, one-line description) is loaded eagerly; full instructions and examples are injected lazily on invocation MCP servers are declared as config and spawned per session, then torn down Shared helper code - a common package or symlinks, not cross-repo relative paths

slides.title: Peter Diamandis - Trillions Sensors Peter Diamandis about
slides.text: Peter Diamandis - Trillions Sensors Peter Diamandis about Visibility, Transparency & Trust A world of radical transparency and a trillion sensors https://metatrends.substack.com/p/visibility-transparency-and-trust The piece argues that a massive, layered “sensor ecosystem” is rapidly covering the planet Driven by satellites, drones, autonomous vehicles, humanoid robots, smartphones, and IoT devices By 2030, tens of billions of connected devices with trillions of sensors will continuously generate data that AI can interpret, creating near-total visibility of the physical world This “radical transparency” could increase accountability, reduce crime, corruption, and even conflict, as people behave differently when observed However, it also poses serious risks to privacy and power balance The key question is whether this transparency benefits everyone equally or enables asymmetric surveillance by those in control
